verdict.rationale: Dagster's official `dagster` Python package is the documented way to build. Code imports it directly (`import dagster as dg`, `@dg.asset`), and pipelines are declared as Python functions. Official integration libraries such as dagster-fivetran and dagster-dlt extend it. However, the evidence shows only a Python authoring library. No OpenAPI spec was found (all candidate paths 404), and nothing documents client SDKs for programmatically driving a Dagster or Dagster+ deployment, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: documented client SDKs for the platform/deployment API, an OpenAPI or REST spec, multi-language SDK coverage, and independent hands-on corroboration of SDK use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: import dagster as dg@dg.assetdef hello(context: dg.AssetExecutionContext):    context.log.info("Hello!")
With Dagster, you declare—as Python functions—the data assets that you want to build.
The dagster-fivetran library provides a FivetranAccountComponent which can be used to easily represent Fivetran connectors as assets in Dagster.
The dagster-dlt library provides a DltLoadCollectionComponent which can be used to easily represent a collection of dlt sources and pipelines as assets in Dagster.
